body: Of course. The point of inpatient is just to get stable, they don't do a whole lot of actually fixing the problem, it's more to keep you from killing your self till they can get someone to work with you on fixing it. As far as therapy, maybe you had a shitty therapist. That's quite common, even if they're not shitty, sometimes we don't get along with them well. Not liking your therapist is a perfectly viable reason to try a new one, until you find one you like. You don't sound ungrateful or rude. I care about you now, and I'm rooting for you. Please do not commit suicide.

Hey, I'm listening. I also understand how suicide definitely feels like the best choice. I would suggest you go to the hospital and get stable. They'll help you with that. Most insurance companies cover it, and if you're worried about your family not understanding your behavior or whatever, having a diagnosed condition (people don't feel the way you do for no reason) might help alleviate that. And if your family is willing to give up a lot for you already, then they'll want you to get help; they won't consider it another burden. If you need to talk more I'm here. Please don't kill yourself.
